skill.name: frontend-design
skill.description: Creates distinctive, production-grade frontend components, pages, and applications. It guides visual direction, implementation choices, and detailed refinement while avoiding generic interface patterns.
skill.summary: Build polished frontend interfaces with a clear visual direction and working implementation.
skill.author: AJV009

content.value_statement: Generic interfaces fail to express a product's purpose or character. This skill guides deliberate visual direction and polished implementation for frontend components, pages, and applications.
actual_capabilities: Defines a clear visual direction from purpose, audience, tone, and technical constraints.
Produces working frontend code for HTML, CSS, JavaScript, React, Vue, and similar stacks.
Applies cohesive typography, color systems, layout composition, backgrounds, and visual details.
Plans CSS animation, React motion, page transitions, scroll effects, and hover interactions.
Matches implementation complexity to minimalist, maximalist, or other chosen design directions.
limitations: Does not supply bundled fonts, images, icon sets, or other third-party assets.
Does not guarantee accessibility, browser compatibility, performance, or production readiness without testing.
Requires project files and technical constraints before integrating a design into an existing application.
Provides design guidance, not automated visual regression tests or deployment tooling.

use_cases.title: Launch a Product Page
use_cases.description: Create a memorable product page that reflects the audience, brand tone, and chosen frontend stack.

use_cases.title: Refresh an Application Interface
use_cases.description: Modernize an existing interface while preserving framework constraints and producing functional, cohesive components.

use_cases.title: Explore a Visual Concept
use_cases.description: Translate an aesthetic direction into an interactive prototype with intentional typography, color, motion, and composition.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Single Component
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a [component] for [audience] using [framework]. Use a [tone] direction, include responsive states, and keep the implementation within [constraints].
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for one focused interface element.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Responsive Page
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a responsive [page type] for [product]. Define a clear visual direction, then implement the page in [stack] with accessible interactions.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request for a complete page with defined product context.

prompt_templates.title: Refresh an Existing Interface
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the provided [files or screenshots]. Preserve [required behavior], replace generic visual choices, and implement a cohesive redesign using the existing architecture.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced redesign that must respect an established codebase.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Multi-View Application
prompt_templates.prompt: Design and implement [application] for [users] in [framework]. Establish a reusable visual system, responsive views, interaction states, motion, and production constraints.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced application request with shared patterns and multiple workflows.

output_examples.input: Create a responsive pricing page for an independent analytics product with an editorial visual direction.
output_examples.output: A functional pricing page with expressive typography, focused plan comparison, responsive layouts, and restrained motion that supports purchase decisions.

output_examples.input: Redesign an operations dashboard without changing its React data flow or existing actions.
output_examples.output: A cohesive dashboard redesign that preserves behavior, improves information hierarchy, and adds purposeful states for navigation, filters, tables, and actions.

output_examples.input: Build a portfolio for a motion designer using plain HTML, CSS, and JavaScript.
output_examples.output: A distinctive portfolio with an intentional visual system, responsive project presentation, and coordinated loading, scrolling, and hover transitions.

best_practices: Provide the audience, purpose, framework, technical constraints, and required behavior before implementation begins.
Choose one coherent visual direction and apply it consistently across typography, color, spacing, motion, and composition.
Test generated interfaces for accessibility, responsiveness, performance, and browser behavior before release.
anti_patterns: Do not request a distinctive result without supplying product context, audience needs, or technical constraints.
Do not add extensive animation when it conflicts with usability, performance, accessibility, or the selected visual direction.
Do not replace established project architecture solely to achieve a visual effect.

faq.question: What can this skill build?
faq.answer: It can guide and implement frontend components, pages, applications, and interface redesigns using common web technologies.

faq.question: Which frontend frameworks does it support?
faq.answer: The guidance covers HTML, CSS, JavaScript, React, Vue, and comparable frontend stacks.

faq.question: Can it work within an existing codebase?
faq.answer: Yes. Provide the relevant files, architecture, behavior requirements, design constraints, and available libraries.

faq.question: Does it guarantee accessible output?
faq.answer: No. Include accessibility requirements and verify keyboard use, semantics, contrast, motion preferences, and assistive technology behavior.

faq.question: Does it provide fonts and visual assets?
faq.answer: No. It can recommend their use, but asset licensing, sourcing, installation, and delivery remain project responsibilities.

faq.question: How should I request a specific visual style?
faq.answer: Describe the audience, purpose, desired tone, reference qualities, required content, and styles that should be avoided.
